+/// Write an executable stub named `binary` into a temp `fake-bin/` dir and
+/// return a PATH with it prepended, so provider-presence checks resolve
+/// without a real install on the host (CI runners have no agent CLIs).
+pub fn prepend_fake_cli_to_path(temp: &TempDir, binary: &str) -> String {
+    let bin = temp.path().join("fake-bin");
+    fs::create_dir_all(&bin).expect("fake bin dir");
+    let path = bin.join(binary);
+    fs::write(&path, "#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n").expect("fake cli");
+    #[cfg(unix)]
+    {
+        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
+        fs::set_permissions(&path, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755)).expect("chmod");
+    }
+    format!(
+        "{}:{}",
+        bin.display(),
+        std::env::var("PATH").unwrap_or_default()
+    )
+}
+

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-06-09 22:28:16Z)**_

All four touched paths are test infrastructure: `Makefile` (build harness), `crates/deadreckon/tests/common/mod.rs` (test helper module), `crates/deadreckon/tests/lifecycle.rs` (integration test), and `crates/deadreckon/tests/orchestrate.rs` (integration test inside `tests/`).

Per the review instructions, test/mock files are explicitly excluded from findings. The changes themselves are also benign in nature:

- **Makefile**: Switches `SHELL` from `/bin/zsh` to `/bin/bash` for `make` recipes — affects only the developer/CI build runner, no runtime attack surface.
- **tests/common/mod.rs**: Adds a helper that writes a no-op shell stub (`#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n`) into a `TempDir`-owned `fake-bin/` and prepends that directory to a returned `PATH` string. Files are written under the per-test `TempDir`, mode `0o755`, and the function returns the string — it does not mutate the process environment globally. No path-traversal vector (binary name is a hard-coded literal in the only caller), no injection (the returned `PATH` is only passed to `.env("PATH", ...)` on a `Command` builder in a test).
- **tests/lifecycle.rs**: Single caller of the helper above, passing the literal `"codex"`.
- **tests/orchestrate.rs**: After `git init` in a test cwd, runs `git -C <cwd> config user.email/user.name` with hard-coded literal values. No attacker-influenced data.

Nothing reaches a production code path, an externally reachable sink, or a CI-trust boundary (no workflow_dispatch / pull_request_target changes, no allowlist edits, no auth/RBAC).
